segments.t: Late in the evening at the ASK offices, Andrea and Hicham reflect upon Mathias's abrupt departure. Acknowledging his personal priorities, Hicham reveals he is moving to London and makes Andrea a life-changing offer. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Il m'a fait de la peine.
Pour un peu, il nous manquerait.
Mon fils a besoin de moi.
J'ai besoin de quelqu'un de confiance.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
'It will be strange without Mathias.' Andrea reflects on the agency atmosphere after Mathias leaves. The future tense 'it' expresses prospective feeling.
Il m'a fait de la peine.
'I felt sorry for him.' Andrea expresses genuine compassion for their fallen senior partner. The idiom 'made' means to cause sorrow or pity.
Pour un peu, il nous manquerait.
'Almost makes you miss him.' Hicham confesses with a hint of warmth that Mathias will be missed. The conditional 'would be missed' indicates a hypothetical feeling.
'Well, I am heading out now.' Hicham prepares to leave the office for the night. The verb 'to leave' means to leave or depart.
'Can you lock up the shop?' Hicham asks Andrea to lock the premises. The colloquial expression 'to close' means to close down the business for the night.
'No problem with that.' Andrea accepts the responsibility easily. The phrase 'no' signals casual agreement.
'You could run the shop.' Hicham expands the metaphor to running the entire agency. The verb 'to run' means to manage or lead.
'I am moving to London.' Hicham announces his impending move across the Channel. The proper noun 'London' designates the British capital.
Mon fils a besoin de moi.
'My son needs me.' Hicham explains his personal reason for stepping back from day-to-day operations. The idiom 'has' expresses necessity.
J'ai besoin de quelqu'un de confiance.
'I need someone trustworthy.' Hicham stresses the paramount importance of integrity in management. The noun phrase 'quelqu'un de confiance' means a trustworthy person.
'I am looking for a new director.' Hicham describes the executive vacancy. The feminine noun 'managing director' designates a female managing director.
'Does the director post interest you?' Hicham presents Andrea with the ultimate promotion. The verb 'interests' takes an indirect object pronoun.
'That is an incredible offer, Hicham.' Andrea is stunned by the magnitude of the proposal. The adjective 'incredible' highlights how extraordinary the offer is.

'Think carefully about this opportunity.' Hicham encourages her to weigh the decision. The imperative 'think' invites thoughtful deliberation. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Pour un peu, il nous manquerait.

J'ai besoin de quelqu'un de confiance.

Andrea stands in the darkened office, overwhelmed by the prospect of taking full command of ASK. From junior agent to managing director, her journey mirrors the evolving spirit of the agency. Now, let's review the scene one last time.
